name: Mei Fong Tan
bio:
Mei Fong Tan has been immersed in the world of IT since the early days of personal computing. After graduating from the National University of Singapore with a degree in Computer Science, she spent several years in the financial sector, optimizing trading systems. However, her true passion always lay in motorsport, fueled by her childhood memories of watching Formula 1 races with her father. She made the jump to motorsport a decade ago, bringing her rigorous approach to data management and system reliability. 

At Triple Eight Race Engineering, Mei Fong oversees all IT infrastructure, ensuring the seamless operation of everything from race strategy simulations to communication networks. She is driven by the belief that efficient data analysis and robust systems are critical to gaining a competitive edge. Mei Fong is known for her meticulous planning, anticipating potential system failures, and implementing preventative measures. Her colleagues often remark on her ability to translate complex technical jargon into easily understandable terms, making her a valuable bridge between the IT department and the rest of the team.

What sets Mei Fong apart is her ability to anticipate the future needs of the team. She's always looking for innovative solutions to improve data processing and security, ensuring that Triple Eight Race Engineering remains at the forefront of technological advancements in motorsport. Her proactive approach and dedication to excellence make her an invaluable asset to the team.

physical.hairStyle: Shoulder-length, straight hair with subtle graying at the temples, usually tied back in a practical ponytail.
physical.description: Mei Fong has a warm, intelligent face, framed by sensible glasses and a pragmatic hairstyle.

quirks: Always carries a small, well-worn notebook filled with system diagrams and handwritten notes.
Insists on a specific brand of green tea, which she believes enhances her focus.
Has a habit of tapping her pen rhythmically when deep in thought, sometimes driving her colleagues slightly crazy.
